description: nf-core/viralrecon samplesheet context, aligned to the pinned 3.0.0 nextflow_schema.json and assets/schema_input.json. Viral genome assembly and intrahost variant calling.

platform.help: REQUIRED in practice. Selects an entirely different sub-workflow. No default — it must come from the user.

protocol.help: REQUIRED in practice. Amplicon runs primer trimming that metagenomic does not; getting it wrong silently distorts variant calls.

genome.help: Viral reference key (e.g. 'MN908947.3' for SARS-CoV-2). NOT a host genome.

fasta.help: Explicit viral reference FASTA; preferred on Luria.

skip_kraken2.help: TRUE by curated default. The host-removal Kraken2 step defaults to an S3 database; skipping avoids an unnecessary download on a cluster with no S3 credentials configured.

required_user_params.name: platform
required_user_params.definition: Which sequencing platform produced this cohort. viralrecon runs a completely different sub-workflow for each, and the schema gives it no default.

required_user_params.name: protocol
required_user_params.definition: How the viral library was prepared. 'amplicon' means tiled PCR primers across the genome (e.g. ARTIC) and triggers primer trimming; 'metagenomic' means untargeted shotgun. Choosing wrongly does not error — it leaves primer sequence in the reads, which distorts variant frequencies.

required_user_params.name: primer_set
required_user_params.definition: Which tiled primer scheme was used, so the right primer coordinates can be trimmed. Only asked for amplicon libraries.

pipeline.name: nf-core/viralrecon
pipeline.core_rule: Columns are sample, fastq_1, fastq_2, barcode. Only `sample` is schema-required, because the nanopore route identifies reads by barcode rather than by FASTQ path. For an Illumina cohort, fastq_1 is required in practice.
pipeline.reference_requirement: A VIRAL reference, via --genome or --fasta. The 3.0.0 schema declares genome and fasta but NO gtf. Note this is the virus, not the host — do not let the cohort's host species drive it.

validation_rules: platform and protocol must be answered by the user. Neither has a default and both change the analysis.
The reference is the VIRUS, not the host. Do not resolve it from the sample's organism metadata — that names the host.
Do NOT pass --gtf: the 3.0.0 schema has no gtf parameter.
primer_set / primer_set_version apply only when protocol=amplicon; leave them unset for metagenomic.
barcode is for the nanopore route only. NExtSEEK holds no nanopore data, so leave it blank.
notes: NO MATCHING DATA IN NExtSEEK as of 2026-08-05: only 19 of 51,359 samples mention SARS / COVID / influenza / virus / viral, and none is a registered viral sequencing cohort. Catalogued so the capability exists if viral work is registered later. viralrecon is one of the most-used nf-core pipelines in the world, so this is a cheap bet.

sources.label: nf-core/viralrecon nextflow_schema.json @ 3.0.0
sources.notes: Authoritative: platform and protocol are enums with no default; genome and fasta declared, no gtf.

sources.label: nf-core/viralrecon assets/schema_input.json @ 3.0.0
sources.notes: Authoritative columns: only `sample` required; fastq_1/fastq_2/barcode optional.

samplesheet_columns.description: Column-level field dictionary for the nf-core/viralrecon input sheet.

barcode.validation_hints: Leave blank — no nanopore data exists here.

report_writer_guidance.purpose: Build an nf-core/viralrecon sheet from a resolved D.SEQ cohort of viral libraries.
report_writer_guidance.workflow_role: Selected for viral genome reconstruction and intrahost variant calling.
population_priority: Ask the user for platform and protocol before anything else; configure_run will refuse without them.
Establish which VIRUS the reference should be. The sample's organism metadata names the host and is the wrong answer.
One row per D.SEQ leaf; barcode blank.
final_checks: The reference is a viral genome, not a host genome.
primer_set is set if and only if protocol=amplicon.
